````text
# #4493: Patch: big set pieces fit a phone's memory, and a layer budget keeps every future animation inside it
Opened by @MaxGoetzmann.

### What it does

On phones, the largest animations, a Mythic's takeover above all, make the browser reload the page. The diagnosis points to the browser killing the tab for memory. iOS WebKit (Safari, and every browser on iOS) reloads a page whose process goes over its memory limit. Chrome on Android does much the same when its renderer is killed for low memory. No JavaScript error is thrown. This was not reproduced on a device: the cloud session that diagnosed it had no iPhone or GPU. The measurements below come from headless Chromium.

**Why.** The effects canvas is capped at 2× pixel density (`fx/surface.ts`, `FX_MAX_DPR`). The DOM cues have no such cap. Every one of them is promoted to its own GPU layer (`.fx-dom > * { will-change: transform, opacity }`, `fx/fx.css:70-76`), and each layer is stored at the phone's full density. On a 3× iPhone that is 9 times the pixels of the same layer at 1×. The phone checks we have measure frame time only (R2803000's five scenes, R3351000's and R3674000's shed ladder), and the ladder never sheds a set piece's main beats. Nothing measures memory. The spike lands within a frame or two of the takeover mounting, so no slow-frame window trips before the tab dies.

**Measured** (headless Chromium, the `/dev/hotseat?seed=42` board, a real `mountDomEffect` takeover for Core #100 Ceaseless Void with its 7 diorama slices, read through CDP `LayerTree` and memory-infra dumps):

| | Board idle | During the takeover |
|---|---|---|
| Composited layer area, in screens' worth (iPhone 13, 3×) | 5.9 | 21.3 |
| That area at 3× density | ~53 MB | ~190 MB |
| `gpu/shared_images` (iPhone 13 / Pixel 7) | 27 / 35 MB | 80 / 109 MB |
| `cc/tile_memory` (iPhone 13 / Pixel 7) | 14 / 19 MB | 64 / 83 MB |

Mounting and removing 5 takeovers in a row brings the layers back to the board's level each time, so this is a spike, not a leak.

**The offenders**, largest first:
1. **The takeover stage** (`fx/dom.ts:79-97`, `fx/fx.css:2465-2472`, `2530`). Each diorama slice (7–8 of them, R3350000) or depth plane (4, R3345000) is its own layer at 120% of the window each way (`inset: -10%`), with `will-change: transform`, under a `perspective` parent. That is about 1.44 screens per slice and about 10 screens for a diorama. `fx-takeover-fly` scales the near slices up to 1.6×, and WebKit renders a layer at its largest animated scale, which costs the nearest slice up to 2.5× more.
2. **The takeover's rays** (`fx.css:2931`): a 120vmax square scaled to 1.2×, about 2.5 screens as one layer.
3. **The takeover's shockwave** (`fx.css:2968-2988`): a 40vmax box with blurred shadows animated to `scale(5)`. The void look's sweep goes to `scale(6)` (`fx.css:2665`).
4. **The Big Crunch collapse** (`fx.css:10542`): a 160vmax circle with a 40vmax border and a 200px inset shadow, from `scale(1.4)`.
5. **They stack.** The stage mounts only when the Mythic's play also holds a set piece (`fx/takeover.ts:231`), so the set piece's own layers (vortex, fold, rift, Terminus shapes) land in the same frames.
6. **The full-screen `img.fx-takeover-art`** (R3407000) and the scene drawings (R3402000) add more full-window layers to the looks that have them.

**What to build**

A. **Trim the offenders** so the looks read the same on a phone at a fraction of the memory:
- Take `will-change` off `.fx-takeover-plane`; the animation promotes it while it runs. Take the plane's overscan down from `inset: -10%` to what its largest dolly actually shows.
- On a phone viewport (the `FX_MOBILE_WIDTH` the particle cap already uses), a diorama's stage draws at most a named constant of layers by merging adjacent slices into one picture, for example far / middle / near. The motion becomes three depths instead of seven and no picture is lost. The four-plane stage holds the same cap.
- Size the rays, the shockwave, the void sweep and the Big Crunch collapse so their box at their largest scale covers no more than the window needs, and retune the masks and stops so the visible look is unchanged. R2803000 already did this once for the rays: 220vmax went to 120vmax with the mask scaled to match.
- Measure every other DOM cue the same way (each set piece shape, the Anomaly rift, the Starship cinematic, the Battleship, the signature figures). Trim any cue that goes over the budget in B.

B. **A layer budget that keeps future animations inside it.** This is the check that stops the next big animation from bringing this back:
- **At run time.** The director keeps a running estimate of the layer memory its mounted DOM cues hold: each promoted element's box × its largest keyframe scale² × the device pixel ratio² × 4 bytes. Before mounting a cue that would pass `FX_PHONE_LAYER_BUDGET_MB` (a named constant, CLAUDE.md rule 9) on a phone, it mounts the cue's optional parts at reduced form, in a fixed order: the stage's slices merged, then the takeover art, then the stage dropped to the dark and the sweep. A set piece's main beats still always mount (R3351000). Where `navigator.deviceMemory` is present and low, the phone budget applies at any width.
- **Per pull request** (vitest, in `web`). A test mounts every DOM cue kind through `mountDomEffect`, with the largest case of each: the diorama with the most slices, every set piece shape, every takeover look. It reads each mounted element's size and keyframe scales from `fx.css` with the rule parser `fx/css.test.ts` already has, and fails when any one cue's estimated layer area at a 390×844 viewport and 3× density passes the budget. It also fails when any single element's extent at its largest scale passes a named number of screens. A new cue or a new full-screen part fails here before it ships.
- **Daily** (the component suite, beside `e2e/cypress/component/fx-phone-frame.cy.tsx`). In a real browser at 390×844 and 3× density, play each phone scene and sum the composited area: every element that `document.getAnimations()` targets or that has `will-change`, its `getBoundingClientRect` area × its largest keyframe scale² × the device pixel ratio². Hold each scene to the same budget, so the jsdom estimate cannot drift from real layout.

**Rulings.** This amends R2803000, whose Rejected paragraph ruled out "cutting layers" in favour of trimming counts, shakes and off-screen raster. Merging slices on a phone cuts layers, deliberately, for memory rather than frame time. It also extends R3351000 and R3674000, whose shed ladder reads frame time alone, with a memory budget that never drops a main beat. Each gets a note in this issue's block, with proving tests named after it (CLAUDE.md rule 3).

### Acceptance

- A Mythic takeover with a diorama on a phone viewport (390×844, 3×) holds at most the phone stage's layer cap, and its estimated layer memory stays within `FX_PHONE_LAYER_BUDGET_MB`. Desktop keeps every slice.
- `.fx-takeover-plane` carries no `will-change`, and its overscan is no larger than its largest dolly shows.
- The rays, the shockwave, the void sweep and the Big Crunch collapse each cover no more than the per-element extent limit at their largest scale, and the gallery captures (`fx-gallery-captures.cy.tsx`) still show each look.
- The director's run-time budget reduces optional parts in its fixed order when a mount would pass the phone budget, and never drops a set piece's main beat. Tests cover each step of the order, a low `navigator.deviceMemory`, and desktop being unaffected.
- The per-PR vitest layer-budget test covers every DOM cue kind and fails on a new cue or part over the budget. A fixture cue that is too big proves it fails.
- The daily component spec measures each phone scene's composited area against the same budget.
- R2803000's five phone scenes still hold `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS`.
- Ruling notes amend R2803000 and extend R3351000, each with its proving tests. `cargo jackioh spec check` passes.

### Blocked by, part of

None.

## Steps

1. **`constants.ts`**, after `FX_PHONE_FRAME_BUDGET_MS`. Give each a comment citing its ruling:

   - `FX_PHONE_STAGE_LAYERS = 3`
   - `FX_LAYER_MAX_SCREENS = 3`
   - `FX_LOW_DEVICE_MEMORY_GB = 4`
   - `FX_LAYER_BYTES_PER_PX = 4`
   - `FX_BYTES_PER_MB = 1_048_576`

   Add all six to `S2` in `constants.test.ts`.

2. **`types.ts`:** add `artless?: true` to `FxTakeoverCue`, documented as "R4493001: the budget dropped the look's own art".

3. **`layers.ts`.** Document every export with its ruling.

   **Device and budget**
   - `type FxDevice = { width; height; dpr; memoryGb: number | null }`.
   - `isPhoneViewport(d)`: `Math.min(d.width, d.height) < FX_MOBILE_WIDTH`.
   - `hasLayerBudget(d)`: a phone viewport, or `memoryGb !== null && memoryGb <= FX_LOW_DEVICE_MEMORY_GB`.
   - `layerBudgetScreens(d)`: `FX_PHONE_LAYER_BUDGET_MB * FX_BYTES_PER_MB / (width * height * r * r * FX_LAYER_BYTES_PER_PX)`, where `r = Math.max(1, d.dpr || 1)`. It is `Infinity` for an empty area.
   - `readDevice()`: reads `window`, plus `(navigator as Navigator & { deviceMemory?: number }).deviceMemory`, which is null unless it is a number.

   **`mergeStage(stage, cap)`**
   - Split the n items into `min(n, cap)` contiguous groups whose sizes differ by at most one, with the larger groups nearest: 7 → [2,2,3], 8 → [2,3,3], 4 → [1,1,2].
   - A slice group becomes `{ image: its images nearest first, joined with ", ", plane: group[0].plane, depth: group[0].depth }`.
   - Planes keep their length: a group's first index holds the joined images, and the rest of its indexes hold `""`.
   - When n ≤ cap, return the stage unchanged.

   **Forms**
   - Constants: `TAKEOVER_FULL = 0`, `TAKEOVER_MERGED = 1`, `TAKEOVER_ARTLESS = 2`, `TAKEOVER_BARE = 3`.
   - `takeoverForm(cue, level)` applies these cumulatively:
     - MERGED merges the stage with `FX_PHONE_STAGE_LAYERS`;
     - ARTLESS removes `art` and sets `artless`;
     - BARE sets `stage: null`.
   - `budgetTakeover(cue, held, d)`:
     - returns `cue` itself when the device has no budget;
     - otherwise returns the first form, from `isPhoneViewport(d) ? MERGED : FULL` up to ARTLESS, with `held + cueScreens(form) <= layerBudgetScreens(d)`;
     - failing that, returns the BARE form.

   **Tables** (screens at 390×844, filled in step 12)
   - `FX_TAKEOVER_LOOK_SCREENS: Record<TakeoverLook, { bare; art }>`. `bare` is the root, dark, sweep, rays and wave; `art` is `.takeover-art`, or 0.
   - `FX_TAKEOVER_PICTURE_SCREENS = 1` and `FX_TAKEOVER_STAGE_SCREENS = 1`.
   - `FX_TAKEOVER_FLY_REACH = 0.6`.
   - `FX_TAKEOVER_DOLLY_SCALES = { far: 1.04, middle: 1.1, near: 1.25, nearest: 1.6 }`.
   - `FX_SET_PIECE_LAYER_SCREENS: Record<SetPieceShape, number>`.
   - `FX_CUE_LAYER_SCREENS: Record<Exclude<FxDomCue["kind"], "takeover" | "setPiece">, number>`.

   **`cueScreens(cue)`**
   - A set piece is its shape's entry; every other kind except the takeover is its kind's entry.
   - A takeover is the sum of:
     - `bare`;
     - `art`, unless `artless`;
     - the picture's screens, when it has `art`;
     - with a stage: the stage's screens, plus each slice's `(1 + depth * FX_TAKEOVER_FLY_REACH) ** 2` or each non-empty plane's dolly scale².

4. **`dom.ts`:**
   - In `takeoverStage`'s `ART_PLANES.forEach`, return early on an empty picture.
   - In the takeover case, mount no `parts` and no `drawing` when `cue.artless === true`.
   - Cite both rulings in the header.

5. **`director.ts`:**
   - Add the option `device?: () => FxDevice`. Without one there is no budget.
   - Add `MountedEffect.screens`, set to `cueScreens(cue)` in `mountDom`.
   - Add `isDomCue(cue): cue is FxDomCue`: not a stage cue, not a canvas cue, not `shake`.
   - Add `budgetDue(due, at)`:
     - It returns `due` unchanged when no takeover is due (checked before reading the device), and when the device is absent or has no budget.
     - Otherwise it replaces each due takeover, in order, with `budgetTakeover(cue, held, device)`. `held` is the sum of:
       - the `screens` of mounted effects with `expiresAt > at`;
       - the `cueScreens` of this frame's other DOM cues (an earlier takeover counts in its chosen form);
       - the `cueScreens` of pending DOM cues due before this takeover ends.
   - In `onFrame`, call `fireDue(budgetDue(due, at), at)`.

6. **`FxLayer.tsx`:** add `device: () => FxDevice` to `FxSeams`, and pass `device: s.device ?? readDevice`. The other directors (stats, packs, `/dev/fx`) get no device.

7. **`fx.css`.** Give each change a comment citing R4493000 and stating its extent.
   - `.fx-takeover-plane`: delete `will-change` and set `inset: 0`. The dollies only scale up, about the centre, and the far dolly's 1.04vw shift stays inside its 2vw of growth.
   - `.fx-takeover-rays`: `width: 92vmax`, mask stops `var(--pal-black) 43%, transparent 130%` (×120/92, the same disc), and update its comment.
   - `.fx-takeover-wave`: `width: 23vmax`.
   - `fx-takeover-collapse` 0%: `scale(5)`.
   - `.fx-setPiece-collapse`: `width: 83vmax`, `border: 20.75vmax`, inset shadow `104px 31px`.
   - `fx-set-piece-fold` 0%: `scale(1.7)`.

8. **`starship.ts`:**
   - Add `phoneZoom: 1.15` to `STARSHIP_CINEMATIC`.
   - Add `zoomMax` to `Ctx`. `planStarship` sets it to `phoneZoom` when `env.compact`, else `Infinity`.
   - In `cinematicCue`, `zoom = Math.min(tune.zoom, c?.zoomMax ?? tune.zoom)` feeds `cameraFrom`, `cameraTo` and `zoom`.

9. **`cssSheet.ts`:** move `Rule`, `Sheet`, `closingBrace`, `splitTop`, `parseDecls`, `nest`, `walk`, `parseSheet` and `keyframeBodies` out of `css.test.ts` verbatim. Export all of them except `nest` and `walk`.

10. **`layerEstimate.ts`:** export `estimateLayers(sheet, root, view)`, which returns `{ label, width, height, scale, screens }[]`, and `layerProblems(name, parts, view, dpr): string[]`.

    **Walk**
    - Visit `root` and its descendants. Skip SVG descendants (`ownerSVGElement !== null`) and any subtree whose `display` is `none`.
    - Treat each `::before` or `::after` that has `content` as a child part.

    **Cascade**
    - Consider only rules whose selector contains `.<element class>` or `[data-fx`, or is `.fx-dom > *`.
    - Match them with `el.matches()`, after stripping a trailing pseudo-element.
    - Skip reduced-motion rules. Throw on any other `@media`, and on any selector `matches` rejects.
    - Later rules win, then inline style. An `animation` declaration clears an earlier `animation-name`.

    **Promoted:** `will-change` other than `auto`, or an animation whose stops set `transform`, `scale`, `translate`, `rotate` or `opacity`. An animation is any `animation` token that is a `keyframeBodies` key, or `animation-name`.

    **Box**
    - The containing block is the parent's box, or the view for `root` or `position: fixed`.
    - For each axis, take the first of these that applies:
      1. its own declaration;
      2. both insets;
      3. `aspect-ratio`;
      4. text content (`content: attr(x)` or a string, or its own text nodes): chars × 0.6em wide and 1.2em tall at the cascaded `font-size`, else 16px;
      5. if absolutely positioned (every cue part and pseudo-element is): the largest box among its pseudo-elements and children that does not depend on its own size, else 0. Any other element takes the containing block.
    - Then clamp with `min-*` and `max-*`.
    - Lengths may be px, %, vw, vh, vmin, vmax, em or rem, inside `calc`, `min`, `max`, `clamp` or `var(--x, fallback)`. Custom properties come from the element, then its ancestors, inline style before rules. Anything else throws, naming the value.

    **Scale:** the largest absolute value among 1, any static `transform` or `scale`, and every stop's `scale()`, `scaleX()`, `scaleY()`, `scale3d()`, `matrix()` (hypot of its columns) or `scale:`. A part's `screens = (w·s)(h·s)/(view area)`.

    **`layerProblems`** lists each part over `FX_LAYER_MAX_SCREENS`, and the cue if Σ screens × view area × dpr² × `FX_LAYER_BYTES_PER_PX` passes the budget in bytes.

    Name 0.6, 1.2 and 16 as constants.

11. **`layerBudget.test.ts`:**
    - **Setup:** a 390×844 view at dpr 3. Mount into `div.fx-dom` with `mountDomEffect`. Boxes: AT `{161,470,68,94}`, FROM `{20,140,68,94}`, TO `{300,620,68,94}`.

      - every `SetPieceShape`, the Terminus ones with beats;
      - every `FX_FIGURES`;
      - each launch, ship and cinematic size, the cinematic at `STARSHIP_CINEMATIC.phoneZoom`;
      - one prismatic takeover with a merged four-plane stage;
      - three takeovers for every `TAKEOVER_TINTS` key:
        - `{ stage: null, artless: true }`;
        - `{ stage: null }`;
        - the phone form: `mergeStage` of the `DIORAMAS` entry with the most slices (images `url(s<i>)`), plus `art: "data:,"` for the `TAKEOVER_ART_LOOKS`.

12. **Fill the tables.**
    - Run with every value at 0. The failures list the estimates.
    - Set each value to its largest estimate, rounded up to 2 decimals. A look's `bare` comes from the artless case, and its `art` is the plain case minus `bare`.
    - Trim any element still over `FX_LAYER_MAX_SCREENS` as in step 7. Never raise a constant.
    - Expect the merged takeovers to come to about 16.3 screens at most (the budget is 17.7), and the radial elements to 2.6–2.9.

13. **`fx-phone-layers.cy.tsx`:**
    - **`beforeEach`:**
      - `cy.viewport(390, 844)`;
      - `Cypress.automation("remote:debugger:protocol", { command: "Emulation.setDeviceMetricsOverride", params: { width: 0, height: 0, deviceScaleFactor: 3, mobile: true } })`;
      - assert `win.devicePixelRatio === 3`.
    - **`afterEach`:** `Emulation.clearDeviceMetricsOverride`, plus `fx-phone-frame`'s settings reset.
    - **Scenes:** copy `mountScene`, `removals` and the events of these scenes from `fx-phone-frame.cy.tsx`: Twisting Nether, meditative-049's takeover, the takeover through Ceaseless Void's diorama, Ceaseless Void's fold, the Starship launch, the Drone Battleship arrival and the Anomaly cast. Add The Big Crunch (`stinkyscape-004-6`) through `galleryPlayOf`/`galleryCardEvents`, as the Felinor scene does.
    - **Measure:** on each rAF for 2000 ms, read the parts under `[data-testid="fx-dom"]`.
      - A part is a target of `document.getAnimations()`, or anything whose computed `will-change` is not `auto`. Read a pseudo-element through `getComputedStyle(target, effect.pseudoElement)`, and skip SVG descendants.
      - Its area is `offsetWidth × offsetHeight` (`clientWidth`/`clientHeight` for an `svg`).
      - Its scale is the hypot of the computed `transform` matrix × the computed `scale`. Keep each part's maximum.
    - **Assert:**
      - every part is within `FX_LAYER_MAX_SCREENS`;
````
